title: The Clay Jebena
style_block: cinematic 35mm Kodak Portra film still, warm golden-hour sunlight filtering through smoke, shallow depth of field, rich terracotta and espresso tones, subtle film grain, intimate documentary realism
character_description: Emaye, a warm Ethiopian grandmother in her 70s with close-cropped silver hair, kind deep-set dark eyes, gentle laugh lines, weathered hands, wearing a traditional white handwoven cotton netela shawl with a subtle woven gold-and-crimson border
tts_style: warm, unhurried, and intimate, like an elder sharing a cherished memory over morning coffee
music_cue: gentle Ethiopian krar and soft washint flute over warm ambient strings, slow 72 BPM, nostalgic and tender, swelling softly in the final 15 seconds

shots.reason: Establish the highland dawn setting and sensory quiet before the ceremony begins
shots.narration_text: Before the sun climbs over the highland ridge, our house always wakes to the scent of green grass and glowing charcoal.
shots.subtitle_en: Before the sun climbs the ridge, our house wakes to fresh grass and charcoal.
shots.image_prompt: Wide establishing view of a misty Ethiopian highland courtyard at dawn, golden morning light touching an earthen home, fresh green grass scattered across a woven reed mat in the center foreground, wisps of woodsmoke rising softly

shots.reason: Introduce Emaye in her element, anchoring emotional warmth and visual character consistency
shots.narration_text: My grandmother Emaye never owned a watch. She measured every morning by the crackle of raw coffee beans darkening in an iron pan.
shots.subtitle_en: Emaye never owned a watch; she measured dawn by roasting coffee beans.
shots.image_prompt: Medium portrait of Emaye seated on a low wooden stool in a sunlit courtyard, gently shaking a dark iron pan of roasting coffee beans over a small clay brazier, soft golden rim light on her white cotton netela shawl

shots.reason: Reveal the central heirloom — the black clay jebena — as the physical symbol of family continuity
shots.narration_text: Beside her sat a black clay jebena, its spout worn smooth by forty years of pouring patience into tiny porcelain cups.
shots.subtitle_en: Beside her sat a black clay jebena, worn smooth by forty years of care.
shots.image_prompt: Intimate close-up of Emaye's weathered hands holding a traditional round black clay Ethiopian jebena coffee pot over glowing embers, tiny hand-painted porcelain cini cups arranged neatly on a low wooden tray below

shots.reason: Evoke memory of community and belonging through the ritual of frankincense smoke
shots.narration_text: When the frankincense rose in silver ribbons, neighbors did not need an invitation. They simply followed the warmth to our doorway.
shots.subtitle_en: When frankincense rose, neighbors followed the warmth straight to our door.
shots.image_prompt: Medium shot of Emaye placing a pinch of golden frankincense onto glowing embers in a small clay burner, luminous ribbons of fragrant smoke curling upward through a sunbeam in the doorway of an earthen home

shots.reason: Introduce the tension of departure — leaving the highland home for a distant city
shots.narration_text: Years later, the morning I packed my suitcase for a city across the sea, the room felt too quiet and the road ahead too wide.
shots.subtitle_en: The morning I packed for a distant city, the room felt quiet and the road wide.
shots.image_prompt: Quiet interior shot of a worn canvas suitcase resting on a woven rug near a wooden doorway looking out onto misty highland hills, morning shadows stretching across the clay floor, muted warm tones

shots.reason: Turning point: Emaye's calm reassurance during the final coffee pour
shots.narration_text: Emaye lifted the jebena high, pouring a thin dark arc without spilling a single drop. Wherever you go, she whispered, never rush the first cup.
shots.subtitle_en: She poured a thin dark arc: Wherever you go, never rush the first cup.
shots.image_prompt: Medium close-up of Emaye lifting the black clay jebena gracefully high to pour a thin, glistening stream of dark coffee into a small porcelain cup, steam rising in warm golden-hour backlight

shots.reason: Emotional peak: passing the heirloom clay jebena from elder hands to younger hands
shots.narration_text: Before I stepped onto the gravel road, she wrapped the clay pot in a folded cotton cloth and pressed it gently into my hands.
shots.subtitle_en: She wrapped the clay pot in cotton cloth and pressed it into my hands.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up of Emaye's weathered hands wrapping the black clay jebena in a clean white woven cotton netela and gently placing it into the outstretched hands of her young granddaughter, warm golden sunlight illuminating their hands

shots.reason: Bridge past and present: showing the tradition alive in a new city apartment
shots.narration_text: Now, oceans away, whenever the winter light turns gray, I roast a handful of beans and listen for the old familiar crackle.
shots.subtitle_en: Now, oceans away, I roast a handful of beans and listen for that crackle.
shots.image_prompt: Warm interior of a modern city apartment window at dusk, the same traditional black clay jebena and two small porcelain cups steaming on a wooden table in the center foreground, soft city lights blurred outside the window

shots.reason: Closing visual resonance and lasting feeling of pride, warmth, and carried heritage
shots.narration_text: Home is not only the ground you leave behind. It is every quiet ritual you carry forward.
shots.subtitle_en: Home is not only where you leave. It is every quiet ritual you carry forward.
shots.image_prompt: Wide serene closing shot of the Ethiopian highland village bathed in amber sunset light, gentle golden clouds above the ridges, peaceful and timeless horizon
